title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives says Congress should not give extra money or special regulatory help to companies or banks that are close to failure because of problems in the AI market. Instead, the focus should be on helping every American who has been harmed by these financial issues.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 aims to establish guidelines and standards for AI development to ensure safety, transparency, and accountability. It encourages research into robust AI systems and requires oversight to prevent harmful outcomes.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to openly disclose how it uses artificial intelligence, detailing the data sets, decision‑making processes, and oversight mechanisms in place. It also mandates regular audits and clear explanations so veterans can understand, question, and challenge any AI‑driven outcomes that affect them.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is a proposed law that aims to regulate how artificial intelligence systems are used in processing veterans’ claims, ensuring they operate fairly, transparently, and responsibly. It seeks to establish clear standards for AI decision-making, oversight mechanisms, and liability provisions so veterans receive accurate, unbiased outcomes from automated systems.

title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act is a proposed law aimed at protecting the integrity of elections by addressing the risks posed by AI-generated misinformation and manipulation. It seeks to regulate the creation, distribution, and use of AI tools that could deceive voters or influence election outcomes, ensuring transparency and accountability in political communication.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is designed to keep people safe from misleading or deceptive AI-generated content by making companies disclose when AI is used and how it might affect consumers. The law also sets clear rules and penalties to make sure companies follow the rules, giving consumers a way to seek help if they’re tricked or harmed by deceptive AI.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act is a law designed to strengthen the safety and resilience of advanced artificial intelligence systems. It requires thorough security testing, sets up oversight mechanisms, and encourages cooperation between industry and government to address AI‑related risks.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act creates a new task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to tackle security issues caused by artificial intelligence. It outlines the team’s role, powers, and how it will work with other agencies to protect the nation’s critical infrastructure from AI‑related threats.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 establishes a framework for identifying, assessing, and mitigating the potential dangers of AI systems to protect public safety and privacy. It requires developers and users to conduct risk assessments, report findings, and adhere to transparency and accountability standards to ensure AI technologies are deployed responsibly.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 creates rules for the safe and responsible use of AI-powered robots, drones, autonomous vehicles, and other physical systems, ensuring they operate within national safety and ethical standards. It seeks to promote transparency, protect public safety, and encourage collaboration between government, industry, and research institutions to oversee the development and deployment of such technologies.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is a proposed law aimed at safeguarding the integrity of elections by regulating the use of deceptive AI technologies. It seeks to prevent false or misleading AI-generated content that could influence voter behavior or undermine public confidence in the electoral process.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act requires companies that develop AI systems capable of modifying themselves to report their design, safety tests, and performance to regulators. The act also establishes guidelines for continuous oversight, data transparency, and penalties for non‑compliance to ensure these systems remain safe and aligned with public interest.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act aims to prevent the creation and use of AI systems that could pose serious risks to public safety and security. It proposes strict regulatory oversight, mandatory risk assessments, and penalties for non‑compliance to ensure AI technologies remain safe and responsible.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act is a law that temporarily stops the building and operation of new data centers used for artificial intelligence. It aims to give regulators time to study the environmental, economic, and security impacts of large AI data centers before allowing more of them to be constructed.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 establishes a federal board to oversee and investigate incidents where AI technologies pose threats to national cybersecurity. The act outlines the board’s authority, reporting responsibilities, and coordination with other agencies to strengthen security and protect sensitive data.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act aims to guarantee that artificial intelligence benefits all U.S. citizens by promoting fair access, responsible development, and economic opportunity. It establishes guidelines and safeguards to protect privacy, encourage innovation, and support workforce training so AI serves the public good.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires organizations that develop or deploy AI systems to submit regular reports detailing the energy consumption associated with their AI operations. The goal of the act is to promote transparency, help manage the environmental impact of AI, and enable policymakers to set more informed sustainability targets.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 requires that medical decisions and treatments be made by licensed physicians rather than AI systems. It limits the use of AI in clinical practice and mandates that any AI-generated recommendations receive human oversight.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This policy establishes a new Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats inside the Executive Office of the President. Its purpose is to monitor, assess, and respond to risks from AI and other advanced technologies, while also addressing additional related responsibilities.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: The resolution establishes a new Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to oversee AI-related matters. It outlines the committee’s purpose, membership, and authority to shape policy and regulation in the AI field.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 establishes a mandatory framework for assessing the safety and societal impacts of AI systems before they are deployed. It requires detailed risk evaluations, transparent reporting, and oversight by relevant authorities to ensure AI technologies are safe and trustworthy for public use.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed law that aims to establish comprehensive rules for the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence systems in the United States. It focuses on ensuring AI safety, transparency, accountability, and the protection of privacy and fundamental rights while fostering innovation and competitiveness.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is designed to limit the carbon footprint and energy use of large AI systems by setting new efficiency standards. It also requires companies to report their AI-related emissions and offers incentives for adopting greener technologies.
